answer.rationale: With the contract expiring in 14 days, no auto-renew, the line at 94% with no buffer, and the incumbent refusing to reopen price, a full primary switch concentrates catastrophic delivery risk into one irreversible move — memory_c2 supports low-cost-vendor economics but was achieved last year under unknown volume/risk conditions. memory_c4's negotiation lever is blocked this cycle (incumbent already refused), and deferral is unsafe given hard expiry. Adding a second source (memory_c3) is the only candidate that simultaneously reduces single-point-of-failure risk, creates competitive pressure that can support the 18% mandate at next review, and fits within one decision's capacity as a guarded partial-volume allocation. I want memory_c3 verified because it is the load-bearing precedent for dual-sourcing actually holding allocation through constraint; if the archived record shows hidden onboarding cost or qualification burden, the intended action weakens.
